CANDIDATE bd-01M161EEPDV8NMC932KA8AY0QC: 397cce7 on m1/resolution. The bead named ExternalMassReport; I sealed THREE types, because StepMass and LayerPreservation are the same defect in the same two files and all three are mine. That is the rule I proposed two hours ago and then failed to apply to myself - the reviewer finds one, the author owns the rest - so this time I swept before fixing.

WHAT WAS OPEN. All three were public-constructor case classes with no validation at all:
- ExternalMassReport accepted negative, NaN and above-one masses, and a split summing past the whole - "attributed 0.7, unranked 0.7" was a publishable external-mass report of 1.4.
- StepMass accepted more comparable steps than there are steps, and a per-step mass on a route with no steps.
- LayerPreservation accepted a mean with nothing evaluable - the exact state its Option was introduced to prevent, reachable by anyone constructing one directly.

SHAPE, and it is the pattern this repo already uses for Admissibility: a private[align] TRUSTED constructor for the computation that guarantees the invariants by construction, plus a public CHECKED `of` returning Either for everyone else. RecallSignature.compute does not have to handle an Either it cannot fail.

NON-CASE FROM THE START, deliberately. The obvious implementation - case class with a private constructor - is exactly the shape the chief swept 84 of and found 45 forgeable, because the derived Mirror's fromProduct rebuilds the value past `of`. I closed that on PlacementResolution an hour ago; writing it into a new type an hour later would have been the third repetition of the same lesson in one session. A compile-time regression asserts no Mirror is derivable for either report type.

MUTATION PROOFS, three, each alone and reverted: V1 allow the split to exceed the whole -> 1 FAILS. V2 allow comparable > total -> 1 FAILS. V3 revert ExternalMassReport to a case class -> the Mirror assertion FAILS.

ONE THING THE TEST CAUGHT THAT I WANT ON THE RECORD: making the constructor private broke my OWN earlier probe, which called ExternalMassReport(0.1, 0.2) as its positive control. The control stopped compiling, typeChecks went false, and the assertion failed - so a test I wrote to prove an accessor exists correctly told me I had removed the way it was constructed. Positive controls earn their keep in exactly this situation; without it the negative assertions would all still have passed and told me nothing.

EVIDENCE at 397cce7, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 156/156, alignJS 156/156, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 76/76, embedBench 50/50, fixturesJVM 108/108, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmt both green.

Stack on m1/resolution is now six: c63e91b, a0fbf01, cf037ba, 2255628, 0835c08, 397cce7, parent eda2d37. I have not rebased onto the doc-only advances since, per the chief's churn ruling.
